STEP 1 - Scene: A single slice of pizza (appears to be a meat-and-vegetable topped slice with melted cheese, green onion or herb bits, and crumbled meat) on a white square plate, photographed from above.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across, so area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 531 cm^2 (treating as a dinner plate). The pizza slice sits at the upper-right edge of the plate, and it is the only food, so it is part of this meal.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Pizza crust (baked dough, the outer triangular edge)
- Melted cheese
- Crumbled meat (sausage or similar)
- Green onion / herb pieces

STEP 4 - Area: The slice covers a small triangular region, about 8% of the plate area (~42 cm^2) in total.
- Crust: ~2% (~11 cm^2)
- Cheese and toppings: ~6% (~31 cm^2)
These add to ~8%, consistent with the visible footprint.

STEP 5 - Volume: A pizza slice is thick, about 1.5 to 2 cm at the topping pile.
- Crust: 11 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 17 ml
- Toppings and cheese: 31 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 47 ml

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like and cheese/meat density ~0.9 to 1.0 g/ml.
- Crust: 17 ml x 0.9 ≈ 15 g
- Toppings/cheese: 47 ml x 0.9 ≈ 42 g
Total ≈ 57 g. A typical pizza slice of this size is often 90 to 110 g, so the visible portion is probably an underestimate of the thickness; I'll take ~80 g as a compromise between the visible footprint and a typical slice's mass.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Crust (baked dough): ~270 kcal/100 g, so 25 g ≈ 68 kcal
- Cheese and meat topping: ~300 kcal/100 g, so 55 g ≈ 165 kcal
Total ≈ 233 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single slice of meat-topped pizza is plausibly 80 g and about 230 to 270 kcal. Plausible for the visible amount.
